sources.quote: The 107,728 MDRs received by FDA in the four-year period following July 27, 2016, include reports of 428 individual deaths of patients implanted with SCSs between 2005 and 2020.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: FDA's 2020 letter counted death reports across all spinal-cord stimulators; Nevro is named only as one of the device makers, not as the source of the deaths or of an outsized death share.

sources.outlet: NBC News (Implant Files, with AP and ICIJ)
sources.quote: The four biggest makers of stimulators are Boston Scientific Corp., based in Massachusetts; Medtronic, with headquarters in Ireland and the U.S.; Nevro, in Redwood California; and Illinois-based Abbott, which entered the market after its $23.6 billion purchase of St Jude Medical Inc.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: Implant Files story on spinal-cord stimulator injuries; names Nevro as a maker only, no Nevro-specific death-report finding.

notes: No source found reports Nevro's death-report share (168 of 737, 22.8%) or compares it with the rest of product code LGW. Only pattern coverage: FDA's September 2020 letter counting deaths among all spinal-cord stimulator reports, and the 2018 Implant Files. The FDA letter page itself returned 404 on both URL forms tried (search snippet gives 497 death-associated MDRs, July 2016 to July 2020). Individual Nevro MAUDE records fetched (mdrfoi 9818010, 18003033, 6852142) were injury reports, not deaths, so none recorded. No FDA warning letter or 483 to Nevro on complaint handling or MDR reporting turned up. Query 5 ran a second internal search on its own (SEC 10-K hits); logged as one.
